newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt blames Israel for failure of Hebron talks.
newsitem.headline: Egypt blames Israel for failure of Hebron talks.

text.p: Egypt blamed Israel on Sunday for the failure of the latest Israeli-Palestinian talks on the West Bank town of Hebron, saying Israel had taken rigid positions and had tried to put pressure on the Palestinian negotiators.

The Palestinians say the talks are close to a dead end. U.S. special peace envoy Dennis Ross, who was in Cairo on Saturday, is leaving the region because he feels he has done all he can to mediate between the two sides.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, commenting on Ross's decision on Sunday, told reporters:

"There's no dispute that the Israeli government holding to rigid positions incompatible with the original agreement, and the attempt to put pressure on the Palestinian side to accept this, are the reasons for obstructing and delaying an agreement, especially on the next steps."
The talks have hit an impasse less over Hebron than over a timetable for planned Israeli withdrawals after Hebron, the West Bank town at the centre of the talks for months.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's cabinet said late on Saturday that the negotiations had reached a crisis. "The talks are close to a dead end," a cabinet statement added.

It said Israel was violating its 1995 interim peace deal with the Palestine Liberation Organisation by demanding that future withdrawals, due to be completed in largely rural areas by September 1997, be put off until May 1999.

Moussa said that for the Israeli-Palestinian talks to succeed, steps towards Israeli withdrawal must continue according to the agreed timetable and talks on the final status of the Palestinian territories must start.

He had not elaborate on the form Israeli pressure was taking but added: "No amount of pressure, or attempts to divert this process from its course, can succeed because that would delay the peace process and make the atmosphere tense."
"It would also introduce an element increasing the imbalance between the Israelis and Palestinians," he added.
"Although I say the peace process has not gone back to square one, this does not mean there are prospects for reaching the finishing line if things continue like this," he added.
Egypt continues to act as informal sponsor to the Palestinian negotiators and Israel often complains the Egyptians are inciting the Palestinians to delay making a deal.
Egypt has denied this, saying the Palestinians know their interests well enough to look after themselves.
